cards.q: Federal Food and Drugs Act (US): year and aim
cards.a: 1906; prevent sale of adulterated or misbranded food and drugs

cards.q: Sulphanilamide tragedy: year and cause
cards.a: 1937; elixir made with an untested solvent (an antifreeze) killed over 100 people

cards.q: Nuremberg Code: year and origin
cards.a: 1947; after experiments on prisoners in Nazi camps during World War II

cards.q: Nuremberg Code established
cards.a: Informed consent; right to withdraw from an experiment at any time

cards.q: Thalidomide: year first marketed (West Germany, as Contergan)
Thalidomide disaster: year and use for which it was promoted
cards.a: 1962; promoted for morning sickness in pregnant women; babies born without limbs or with severe deformities

cards.q: Declaration of Helsinki: year and issuing body
cards.a: 1964; World Medical Association

cards.q: Declaration of Helsinki: role for ICH-GCP
cards.a: Forms the ethical base of ICH-GCP principles

cards.q: Belmont Report: year and body that wrote it
cards.a: 1979; National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects

cards.q: Law that created the commission behind the Belmont Report
cards.a: National Research Act of 1974

cards.q: CIOMS guidelines: first published and what they apply
cards.a: 1993; applies the Declaration of Helsinki to present-day research

cards.q: Topics that CIOMS guidelines address: list all
cards.a: HIV/AIDS research; availability of study treatment after the study; women as subjects; confidentiality; compensation for adverse events; consent; avoiding unnecessary suffering; risk versus benefit

cards.q: ICH-GCP: year finalised and year effective
cards.a: Finalised 1996; effective 1997

cards.q: Cardinal principle of research on human participants
cards.a: Respect for the dignity of persons

cards.q: Principle of precaution in research
cards.a: Minimum risk to participants and affected community; no known irreversible adverse effects

cards.q: Requirements common to all research guidelines
cards.a: Ethical and scientific review; informed consent

cards.q: WHO-GCP versus ICH-GCP: number of principles
cards.a: WHO-GCP has 14; ICH-GCP has 13 (WHO principles 5 and 6 combined)

cards.q: Which regions ICH-GCP was designed to harmonise
cards.a: US, Japan and EU (drug registration)

cards.q: WHO-GCP was developed for whom
cards.a: Less well-equipped regulatory agencies in countries with no other guideline

cards.q: ICH-GCP principles 1 to 13: list all, in order
cards.a: Ethical conduct; benefit-risk assessment; subjects over science; adequate prior information; scientific validity; independent review; qualified medical care; trained personnel; informed consent; information handling; confidentiality; drug accountability (GMP); quality systems

cards.q: India's first GCP guideline: year and issuing body
cards.a: 2001; CDSCO expert committee

cards.q: Number of ethical principles in the Indian GCP document
cards.a: 10, in line with the Declaration of Helsinki

cards.q: Indian GCP principles named in the text: list all
cards.a: Informed consent; community agreement; non-exploitation; subject privacy and confidentiality; risk minimisation; accountability and transparency of investigators and sponsors; essentiality

cards.q: Principle of essentiality
cards.a: Use human subjects only when absolutely essential and no alternative is available

cards.q: ICMR ethical guidelines for biomedical research on human subjects: year introduced
cards.a: 2000; periodic revision planned

cards.q: Why standard ethical guidelines help research
cards.a: Allow comparison between institutions; prevent duplication or plagiarism of work

cards.q: Vulnerable groups needing extra protection by an ethics committee: list all
cards.a: Hierarchical groups (prisoners, armed forces, medical and other students and staff); patients with incurable disease; unemployed or impoverished; emergency patients; ethnic minorities; homeless persons; nomads; refugees; minors; those unable to consent

cards.q: Sponsor's duty for serious adverse events (SAE): deadline to forward
cards.a: Within 14 days of knowledge of the event, to the licensing authority, ethics committee chair and head of institution

cards.q: Investigator's duty for serious adverse events: report deadline
cards.a: Within 24 hours of occurrence; reason needed if late

cards.q: Investigator's full SAE report deadline to licensing authority, ethics committee and head of institution
cards.a: Within 14 days of occurrence

cards.q: Sponsor's report of compensation paid for trial injury or death: deadline
cards.a: Within 30 days of the order

cards.q: Summary report when a trial is stopped early (e.g. lack of commercial interest)
cards.a: Within 3 months

cards.q: Who pays for medical management and compensation for trial-related injury or death
cards.a: Sponsor, representative or investigator of the centre

cards.q: Ethics committee's duty if it revokes trial approval
cards.a: Record the reasons; tell the investigator and the licensing authority at once

cards.q: Trial sponsor's status reports go to
cards.a: Central Licencing Authority, at the prescribed periodicity

cards.q: NDCT rules: six-monthly trial report submitted to DCGI through which portal
cards.a: SUGAM portal

cards.q: NDCT rules: how often enrolment status goes to DCGI
cards.a: Every 3 months

cards.q: NDCT rules: termination of a trial or BA/BE study notified to the licensing authority within
cards.a: 30 days, with the cause

cards.q: NDCT rules: post-trial access to the drug for participants
cards.a: Sponsor provides free of cost, on investigator recommendation and ethics committee approval

cards.q: NDCT rules: academic trial (solely for research) needs
cards.a: Ethics committee approval only; no DCGI permission; not for promotional or approval use

cards.q: NDCT rules: sponsor's duty for medical care of injured subjects
cards.a: Free medical management as long as the investigator advises, or until injury is shown to be unrelated to the trial

cards.q: NDCT rules: SAE of death reported to DCGI, head of institution and EC chair within
cards.a: 14 days of knowledge of the death

cards.q: ICMR ethics committee for biomedical research: composition rule for members
cards.a: Constituted under ICMR national ethical guidelines

cards.q: ICMR EC members (biomedical and health research): list all
cards.a: Chairperson or vice-chairperson; member secretary; basic medical scientist; clinician(s); legal expert; social scientist, philosopher, ethicist or theologian; lay person

cards.q: Who should not be affiliated with the institution (ICMR EC)
cards.a: The chairperson, and at least one member (preferably the lay person)

cards.q: Who is the member secretary, and what must they know
cards.a: Staff of the institution; experience in clinical research and ethics

cards.q: ICMR EC quorum
cards.a: At least 5 members, medical and non-medical; no decision valid without quorum

cards.q: ICMR EC member training: deadline if not trained at appointment
cards.a: Within 6 months of appointment

cards.q: Documents a member must do or declare for ICMR EC: list all
cards.a: Signed CV and training certificates; declare conflicts of interest; sign confidentiality agreement; name, profession and affiliation public

cards.q: ICMR EC review categories by risk
cards.a: Expedited (minimal risk); full (more than minimal risk, e.g. vulnerable groups); exempt (less than minimal risk)

cards.q: Example of expedited review
cards.a: Clinical studies of drugs and devices already approved

cards.q: Example of exempt review
cards.a: Research on educational practice

cards.q: Periodic review interval for ongoing research
cards.a: Every 6 months up to 1 year

cards.q: Interim review of research under special circumstances
cards.a: By a sub-committee, re-examined by the full committee; quarterly as required

cards.q: Continuing ethics review covers: list all
cards.a: New information; adverse event monitoring; regular follow-up

cards.q: Decisions an ethics committee can reach: list all
cards.a: Outright approval (very minor changes); approval with modifications; resubmit with more information; outright disapproval

cards.q: How ethics committee decisions are preferably reached
cards.a: By consensus; subject experts give opinions but do not decide

cards.q: Minutes of ethics committee meetings
cards.a: Approved and signed by the chair

cards.q: How long trial documents are kept after completion
cards.a: 5 years

cards.q: Documents submitted to the ICMR EC: list all
cards.a: Trial protocol; patient information sheet and consent form with translations; investigator's brochure; PI's CV; insurance or compensation policy; investigator-sponsor agreement

cards.q: Elements an ethics committee reviews in a proposal: list all
cards.a: Rationale and essentiality; specific objectives; design and methods; risk-benefit; participant selection; conflicts of interest; completeness of consent; injury management and compensation

cards.q: Scientific design points reviewed by an ethics committee: list all
cards.a: Design; statistics and sample size; risks and benefits; justification of controls; withdrawal criteria; termination criteria; monitoring and audit; emergency facilities; reporting and publication

cards.q: Clinical trial ethics committee (NDCT rules): minimum membership
cards.a: 7 members, medical and non-medical, scientific and non-scientific

cards.q: Clinical trial ethics committee must include: list all
cards.a: A lay person; a woman member; a legal expert; an independent member (social scientist, NGO representative, philosopher, ethicist or theologian)

cards.q: Share of trial ethics committee members not associated with the institute
cards.a: At least 50%

cards.q: Quorum to review a clinical trial protocol (NDCT rules)
cards.a: At least 5 members, including a medical scientist (preferably a pharmacologist), a clinician, and a legal expert, social scientist, NGO representative or lay person

cards.q: Clinical trial EC registration validity
cards.a: 5 years, unless suspended or cancelled by the Central Licensing Authority

cards.q: Renewal application for clinical trial EC: how early
cards.a: 90 days before expiry

cards.q: Licensing authority decision time on EC renewal
cards.a: Within 45 working days, with reasons in writing

cards.q: Deadline to tell the licensing authority of a change in EC membership
cards.a: Within 30 days

cards.q: Expert advisers at a clinical trial EC meeting have
cards.a: No voting rights

cards.q: Clinical equipoise: definition
cards.a: Genuine uncertainty about which of two or more treatments is better, among experts

cards.q: Argument against placebo-controlled trials
cards.a: Violates clinical equipoise when proven effective therapy exists, and the principle of beneficence

cards.q: Placebo control when an available treatment prevents death or irreversible morbidity
cards.a: Generally inappropriate

cards.q: Conditions in which a placebo-controlled trial is ethically justified (list all)
cards.a: No proven or approved therapy exists; existing therapy of modest or inconsistent efficacy with frequent adverse effects and new drug not expected to be better; patients informed, autonomy kept, monitoring, rescue and escape procedures, GCP followed

cards.q: When a new drug is expected to be no better than a modest, inconsistent existing therapy
cards.a: Placebo control not justified; superiority or non-inferiority design is sufficient

cards.q: OHRP 2008 safeguards for placebo trials: list all
cards.a: Add-on design so all receive standard care; minimum placebo exposure; early-escape and withdrawal rules; smaller placebo arm; DSMB interim review

cards.q: Consent form contents for a placebo-controlled trial: list all
cards.a: Meaning of placebo in lay terms; that placebo may be given; why it is used and the alternatives; duration and discomfort; harm of not getting or delaying effective treatment; the condition may worsen; right to withdraw

cards.q: Placebo use in clinical practice: when ethical
cards.a: Only for the patient's welfare: uncertain course, standard treatment failed or not tolerated, or no effective therapy exists

cards.q: Placebo in clinical practice: what it must never do
cards.a: Replace effective treatment; continue when proven ineffective (stop it immediately)

cards.q: Placebo that helps the patient, when no better treatment exists
cards.a: Stopping it is unethical

cards.q: If asked about a placebo, the physician should
cards.a: Answer honestly about its nature and expected effects

cards.q: Conflict of interest: definition
cards.a: Personal factors that could influence professional roles or judgement, e.g. funding or financial gain

cards.q: What matters most about conflicts of interest
cards.a: Whether they were recognised and managed

cards.q: Burnout: ICD-11 definition, in one phrase
cards.a: Syndrome from chronic workplace stress not successfully managed

cards.q: ICD-11 burnout dimensions: list all
cards.a: Energy depletion or exhaustion; mental distance from job, negativism or cynicism; reduced professional efficacy

cards.q: Who described standard burnout features (1970s)
cards.a: Christina Maslach and colleagues

cards.q: Burnout causes in doctors: list all
cards.a: Workload (long hours, night duty, administrative tasks, patient overload); poor teamwork; lack of reward, autonomy and job security; work-family conflict; lack of resources and development

cards.q: Consequences of burnout: list all
cards.a: More major medical errors and adverse patient incidents; lower patient satisfaction; doctors leave practice; effort-reward imbalance linked to negative health outcomes

cards.q: Traffic-light model
cards.a: Stepwise, colour-coded approach to recognising and assessing medical burnout

cards.q: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction: origin
cards.a: Developed in the late 1970s at the University of Massachusetts Medical Center

cards.q: Burnout prevention: what the text says is needed beyond individual measures
cards.a: System-level changes, in addition to or instead of targeted individual help

cards.q: Pharmacologist's teaching roles: list all
cards.a: Undergraduate (second-year MBBS and BDS); postgraduate, including thesis guidance; nursing and pharmacy students

cards.q: Pharmacology teaching content: list all
cards.a: Rational drug use and essential drugs; drug classes, effects, toxicity, ADRs, interactions; separating real information from promotional claims; dose by age, sex and health; routes of administration

cards.q: Pharmacologist's continuing-education role for doctors: list all
cards.a: Rational use; unbiased information on new drugs; ADR recognition and reporting; drug audit; generic prescribing

cards.q: CBME pharmacology competency code format
cards.a: PH followed by a number, e.g. PH 1.2 (evidence-based medicine and TDM)

cards.q: CBME competency PH 1.64 covers
cards.a: Overview of drug development, phases of clinical trials and good clinical practice

cards.q: CBME competency PH 1.43 covers
cards.a: Rational use of antimicrobials, including antibiotic stewardship programmes

cards.q: CBME competency PH 1.55 covers
cards.a: National health programmes

cards.q: CBME competency PH 1.2 covers
cards.a: Basis of evidence-based medicine and therapeutic drug monitoring

cards.q: Katzung's Indian edition: how CBME competencies are mapped
cards.a: Each PH competency is mapped to the textbook chapter(s) that cover it

cards.q: Belmont Report justice principle: what it says
cards.a: Research should not unduly involve groups unlikely to benefit from its later applications

cards.q: Argument that foreign drug trials breach the justice principle
cards.a: Testing where participants cannot afford the approved product

cards.q: Defenders' reply on foreign drug trials
cards.a: Such trials bring medical care to underserved people

cards.q: WHO rational-use intervention: undergraduate teaching
cards.a: Problem-based pharmacotherapy training

cards.q: WHO rational-use intervention: in-service education
cards.a: Continuing in-service medical education required for licensure

cards.q: Essential medicines 'must know' drugs are for
cards.a: Teaching and training of health care professionals

cards.q: AETCOM: what it is
cards.a: Longitudinal programme for attitude, ethics and communication competence
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: AETCOM booklet: year and issuing body
cards.a: 2018, Medical Council of India
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: AETCOM booklet sections I to V: list all
cards.a: Goals, roles and universal competencies; teaching modules; non-core competencies; competency log; formative elements
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: AETCOM modules per professional year (PY I to IV)
cards.a: 5, 8, 5 and 9 modules
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: AETCOM module hours per professional year (PY I to IV)
cards.a: 34, 37, 25 and 44 hours
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: Roles GMR 2017 adds for the graduate (AETCOM): list all
cards.a: Leader and member of the health care team; communicator; life-long learner; professional
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: AETCOM definition of competency
cards.a: Habitual, judicious use of communication, knowledge, skills, reasoning, emotions, values and reflection
refs: WEB MCI AETCOM Attitude Ethics and Communication competencies booklet 2018 https://nmc.org.in/storage/new/AETCOM_book.pdf

cards.q: MD Pharmacology PG teaching-learning methods: list all
cards.a: Interactive lectures; PBL modules; case discussions; small group discussions; seminars; journal club; research presentations
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: MD Pharmacology PG training: duration
cards.a: 3 years, in 6 terms of 6 months each
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Minimum formal teaching per week, MD Pharmacology PG
cards.a: At least 6 hours, besides laboratory work
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: MD Pharmacology PG log book: purpose
cards.a: Records experiments and skills; aids internal evaluation
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Assessment during training, MD Pharmacology PG
cards.a: Formative: continual, with feedback
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Assessment at end of training, MD Pharmacology PG
cards.a: Summative, under postgraduate examination rules
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: MD Pharmacology PG examination: parts, list all
cards.a: Thesis; theory; practical/clinical
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Minimum marks to pass, MD Pharmacology PG exam
cards.a: 50% in theory and 50% in practical, separately
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Thesis submission timing before theory and clinical exams
cards.a: At least 6 months before
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf

cards.q: Thesis examiners: composition
cards.a: Minimum three: one internal, two external
refs: WEB NMC Guidelines for Competency Based PG Training Programme MD Pharmacology (copy hosted by Narayan Medical College) https://nmch.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/MD-PHARMACOLOGY.pdf
